correctness.rationale: For the unnormalized XOR operator on labelled supports of all permutations, the two restricted-cycle EGFs give the bivariate signed EGF (1+s+t)/sqrt((1-(s+t)^2)(1-(s-t)^2)), where s marks ordinary labels and t marks labels in the Walsh character. In its even part put u=s^2,v=t^2; expansion of ((1-u-v)^2-4uv)^(-1/2) gives the binomial-square coefficient by Vandermonde. The odd part gives the stated two-term recursion with exactly one nonzero term. Restoring labelled factorials proves the multiplier, signs, and parity of the nullspace. On odd orders the even-weight sequence is strictly decreasing, and complement symmetry gives the (n-1)! minimum; n=1 has both multipliers one. On even orders the sign of the successive positive-eigenvalue ratio minus one is the sign of 2r+1-m. Stirling at r=m/2+O(1) yields sqrt(pi*m)/2 for the nonzero-spectrum condition number, not a full inverse. Moore–Penrose and projection conclusions follow by orthonormal Walsh diagonalization. value.rationale: The statistic is naturally induced by cycle parity and the exact law answers a useful inversion question: even sizes lose precisely the odd Walsh modes, whereas invertible odd sizes have a condition number growing faster than the restricted even-size inverse. Exact smallest eigenvalues locate the most poorly recovered modes; the singular-versus-invertible parity transition and the distinct stability scales are not just a computation of total cycle counts.
